key_insight: Random Forest and XGBoost achieved the highest mean scores for rooftop PV shading-fault detection, but operating-condition differences complicate the classifier ranking.
engineering_relevance: PV monitoring systems need episode-aware validation and matched normal-operation data to distinguish shading signatures from time-of-day and output-level effects.
method: Compared seven classical and ensemble-tree classifiers on real sensor data from a 4 kW rooftop PV plant.
Used three repeats of five-fold group-aware nested cross-validation, keeping staged episodes intact.
Applied SMOTE within training folds and Holm correction to 21 pairwise Wilcoxon tests.
evidence_signal: Across 20,800 rows retaining all 17 fault episodes, Random Forest achieved mean accuracy 0.838 and MCC 0.526, yet almost entirely missed four fault episodes.
watch_item: Matched no-fault sampling is needed before generalising the rankings: clock time alone reached MCC 0.44, indicating substantial operating-condition confounding.
paper_title: Benchmarking Classical Machine Learning Models for Shading-Fault Detection in Rooftop Photovoltaic Systems Using Real Sensor Data
